findings.title: Systemic multiple-dependent-claim-on-multiple-dependent-claim violation
findings.attack: Claims 8, 9 (and equivalently 69, 81, 92) are multiple dependent claims; claim 10 and every later 'any one of claims X to Y' claim whose range reaches back past them inherits an improper basis under MPEP 608.01(n)(iii), compounding through 53 of 102 claims.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Renumber/restructure claim dependencies so no multiple dependent claim's range includes another multiple dependent claim; restore any lost combinations as separate singly-dependent claims. No scope need be lost.

findings.title: Reference numerals omitted from claims 79-89
findings.attack: Claims 79-89 name the poppet, sealing face, deflectable ring element, main passage, purge gap and purge flow path without any reference numeral, unlike parallel claims 1, 58, 67 and 90-102, creating an internal inconsistency in claim practice.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the existing reference numerals at first mention in claims 79-89, matching claim 1's practice.

findings.title: Hybrid dependency format in claims 61, 89, 99
findings.attack: Claims 61, 89 and 99 each carry a formal dependency and additionally incorporate a further claim range by reference in the body text ('according to any one of claims X to Y'), leaving ambiguous how the claim should be counted and construed, especially since the incorporated ranges are laden with the F-37-1 defect.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Confirm the intended relationship once F-37-1 is cured; no wording change needed if the intended technique is claim incorporation by reference to a sub-combination.

findings.title: Dangling final clause in independent claims 1 and 58
findings.attack: The shape-recovery clause at the end of claims 1 and 58 is not clearly assigned to the purge state or set apart as a separate transition, inviting a parsing dispute over whether recovery is required and when.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Re-punctuate as a separate 'wherein, when the pressure differential falls...' clause; no scope change.

findings.title: 112(f) exposure in 'deflecting formation' and 'threshold-setting arrangement'
findings.attack: Both terms combine a generic noun with a function only, risking US means-plus-function construction limited to the disclosed corresponding structures and their equivalents, giving a competitor an escape route via an undisclosed equivalent mechanism.
findings.least_narrowing_action: None required; informational for Prompt 33 litigation assessment. Risk already knowingly accepted per terminology lock.

findings.title: 'Chamber side' applied to non-poppet components without antecedent
findings.attack: [0010] defines 'chamber side' only of the poppet; claims 9 and 33 apply 'the chamber side' to the fixed seat and the purge gap respectively without an antecedent covering that usage.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Broaden [0010]'s definition to a general orientation within the valve core rather than a property of the poppet alone (see Prompt 38 Correction); no claim text change needed.

findings.title: 'About'/'approximately' used without a stated tolerance
findings.attack: [0007] confirms 'about'/'approximately' carries no defined tolerance unless separately stated, and none is stated for the 0.03 mm interference or the 1.0/3.5 bar values, risking an EPO clarity objection.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add a stated tolerance in the description rather than deleting the qualifier from the claims.

findings.title: Unenumerated single-sentence state definition in claims 1 and 58
findings.attack: The three states are separated only by semicolons in one continuous sentence, increasing the risk of a clarity objection over which limitations belong to which state.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Enumerate the three states (i)/(ii)/(iii); no scope change.

corrections.from_text: 10. The valve core of any one of claims 1 to 9, wherein the deflectable ring element has a wall arranged such that an axial load applied to the deflectable ring element by the poppet in over-travel is converted into the radial deflection.
corrections.to: [No single text substitution cures this claim in isolation; requires claim-set renumbering so no 'any one of claims X to Y' range includes claim 8 or 9 (or 69, 81, 92), with lost combinations restored as separate claims singly dependent from 8 and from 9.]
corrections.reason: Claim 10 (an MDC) takes claims 8 and 9 (both MDCs) as part of its basis, contrary to MPEP 608.01(n)(iii); recurs at the 52 other claims listed in F-37-1.

corrections.from_text: 79. A method of operating an inflation valve of an inflatable chamber which holds liquid sealant, the inflation valve comprising a poppet having a supply side, a chamber side and a sealing face, a deflectable ring element, a main passage past the sealing face which is closed by the sealing face in a closed state of the inflation valve, and a return spring biasing the poppet towards the closed state, the method comprising, within one inflation event: coupling an inflation device to the supply side and raising a pressure differential between the supply side and the chamber side to at or above a crack pressure, whereby the poppet moves through a normal stroke into a normal-open state in which inflation gas flows through the main passage into the inflatable chamber while the deflectable ring element remains in its at-rest form and a purge gap associated with the deflectable ring element remains closed; raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold higher than the crack pressure, whereby the poppet moves into over-travel beyond the normal stroke and produces a radial deflection of the deflectable ring element, the radial deflection opening the purge gap, and inflation gas flows as an air purge along a purge flow path, separate from the main passage, from the supply side through the purge gap into the inflatable chamber across surfaces on which sealant film accumulates; and removing the inflation device from the supply side, whereby the pressure differential falls and the deflectable ring element undergoes shape recovery to its at-rest form and closes the purge gap.
corrections.to: 79. A method of operating an inflation valve of an inflatable chamber which holds liquid sealant, the inflation valve comprising a poppet (40) having a supply side, a chamber side and a sealing face (42), a deflectable ring element (30), a main passage (64) past the sealing face (42) which is closed by the sealing face (42) in a closed state of the inflation valve, and a return spring (50) biasing the poppet (40) towards the closed state, the method comprising, within one inflation event: coupling an inflation device to the supply side and raising a pressure differential between the supply side and the chamber side to at or above a crack pressure, whereby the poppet (40) moves through a normal stroke into a normal-open state in which inflation gas flows through the main passage (64) into the inflatable chamber while the deflectable ring element (30) remains in its at-rest form and a purge gap (60) associated with the deflectable ring element (30) remains closed; raising the pressure differential above an over-travel threshold higher than the crack pressure, whereby the poppet (40) moves into over-travel beyond the normal stroke and produces a radial deflection of the deflectable ring element (30), the radial deflection opening the purge gap (60), and inflation gas flows as an air purge along a purge flow path (62), separate from the main passage (64), from the supply side through the purge gap (60) into the inflatable chamber across surfaces on which sealant film accumulates; and removing the inflation device from the supply side, whereby the pressure differential falls and the deflectable ring element (30) undergoes shape recovery to its at-rest form and closes the purge gap (60).
corrections.reason: Brings claim 79 into line with reference-numeral practice in claims 1, 58, 67, 90-102; same treatment applies to claims 80-89.

corrections.from_text: ...the radial deflection opening the purge gap so that a purge flow path (62), separate from the main passage, extends from the supply side through the purge gap to the chamber side; the deflectable ring element undergoing shape recovery to its at-rest form and closing the purge gap when the pressure differential falls below the over-travel threshold.
corrections.to: ...the radial deflection opening the purge gap so that a purge flow path (62), separate from the main passage, extends from the supply side through the purge gap to the chamber side; and wherein, when the pressure differential falls below the over-travel threshold, the deflectable ring element undergoes shape recovery to its at-rest form and closes the purge gap.
corrections.reason: Removes ambiguity as to whether shape recovery is part of the purge state's own definition or a separate subsequent transition, without narrowing scope.

assumptions.text: Claim-dependency formalities (37 CFR 1.75(c); MPEP 608.01(n)) assessed primarily against US practice, since no single target jurisdiction is named for this prompt.

'Chamber side'/'supply side' treated as defined only with reference to the poppet per [0010]; claims 9 and 33's broader usage treated as an unintended inconsistency curable by broadening the definition.
No priority document was supplied; antecedent-basis and support findings assessed against the description and claims as filed in this run only.

open_questions.text: Should the claim set be renumbered to cure F-37-1 before or after Prompts 28-29 run, since renumbering will shift every claim reference used there?
Is the omission of reference numerals from claims 79-89 deliberate or an oversight?
Are claims 61, 89 and 99 intended as ordinary dependent claims that also incorporate a further claim range by reference, or is some other relationship intended?
